om: Faste engelske oversættelser af sidens egne længere tekster: guiden Sådan virker siden, dialogerne og Nyt på siden (nyheder.json). Nøglen er den danske tekst præcis, som den står på siden. Hentes kun, når siden vises på engelsk. Ændres en dansk tekst, eller kommer der en ny nyhed, rettes eller tilføjes linjen her. Mangler en linje, står teksten på dansk.

t.Bekræft. Globus åbner nu i sit eget vind: Confirm. Globus now opens in its own window and also works offline.
t.Appen er den samme side. Den gemmer inte: The app is the same page. It stores nothing about you beyond what the page itself remembers in your browser.
t.Siden er en prototype. Her står, hvilke: The page is a prototype. This shows which data we fetch, from where, and when it was last fetched. Everything is fetched automatically from the sources' own feeds and shown as the source wrote it.

t.Kloden viser smitteudbrud, krig og konfl: The globe shows outbreaks, war and conflict, natural disasters and travel advice around the world, so you can see what is happening where you are going. Each dot is an event with sources, and tapping it opens a card with an image, a timeline and further reading.
t.Mistanker om smitteudbrud er hule og sti: Suspected outbreaks are hollow and dashed and appear when you zoom in. War and conflict is based on the media and is marked as such.
t.Et tomt område betyder, at vi ikke har s: An empty area means we have not seen anything. Always read the official travel advice before you travel.
t.Trinnene oversættes efter faste regler f: The levels are translated by fixed rules from the authorities' own scales, not by our judgement.
t.Krig, borgerkrig, væbnede konflikter og: War, civil war, armed conflicts and protests according to the media: where there is fighting, who is in conflict with whom, who provides military support, and who sends aid.
t.GDELT og ca. 240 medier, overskrifter fr: GDELT and about 240 media outlets, headlines from Reuters, AP, CNN and others, OCHA FTS and UNHCR
t.Udbrud af smitsom sygdom med de seks tri: Outbreaks of infectious disease with the six stages from suspicion to new variant.
t.Varsler om hede og kulde i Europa og tør: Warnings of heat and cold in Europe and drought worldwide.
t.Meteoalarm (Europas vejrtjenester, også: Meteoalarm (Europe's weather services, including DMI) and GDACS
t.Skælv fra styrke 5,5 eller med PAGER-var: Earthquakes of magnitude 5.5 or more, or with a PAGER alert, in the last 7 days.
t.Igangværende oversvømmelser og varsler o: Ongoing floods and warnings of flooding and storm surge in Europe.
t.Tropiske cykloner i hele verden og vindv: Tropical cyclones worldwide and wind warnings in Europe.
t.Igangværende skov- og naturbrande og var: Ongoing forest fires and wildfires, and fire danger warnings in Europe.
t.Lande, hvor Udenrigsministeriet beder di: Countries where the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs asks you to take extra care or advises against travel, fully or in part. Where it has no travel advice, the British advice is used. Choose a country to see everything about it.
t.Udenrigsministeriets rejsevejledninger o: The Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs' travel advice and the British Foreign Office (FCDO)
t.Farven fortæller, hvad det er. Størrelse: The colour tells you what it is. The size and the rings tell you how severe it is. When several dots are close together, they merge into one dot with the number, and the edge shows the directions' colours. Zoom in or tap the dot to separate them. The scale has four levels like the Danish travel advice, plus a fifth, acute, for what is new and critical right now. Acute items also appear in the ticker at the bottom. Below the globe you choose the minimum severity to show.
Good to know. Use common sense.
t.Hold øje med det, og forbered dig lidt m: Keep an eye on it and prepare a little more than usual.
Consider whether the trip is necessary.
t.WHO vurderer risikoen som høj: WHO assesses the risk as high
t.Myndighederne fraråder rejser eller har: The authorities advise against travel or have declared an international emergency.
t.Nyt og kritisk lige nu: alvor 4 med en u: New and critical right now: severity 4 with a development within the last three days.
t.Alvor 4 med en ny udvikling inden for tr: Severity 4 with a new development within the last three days
t.Rejsevejledninger har deres eget ikon me: Travel advice has its own icon with a plane. Countries with travel advice from yellow upwards are shaded a tone darker, and regions the advice names are coloured when you zoom in. War and conflict has a dot for each place where the media write about fighting or protests, and a heat map. Tap a dot to see only what has been written about that place. Tap the country itself to open the country page with everything about it, where you can also follow the country.
t.Ved rejsevejledninger står lande med en: For travel advice, countries with advice from yellow upwards are shaded a tone darker. The dot shows the highest level in the country. Which areas it covers is in the details and on um.dk. The Danish ministry only has travel advice for some of the world's countries. For the others, the British Foreign Office (FCDO) level is used: advises against all travel is 4, advises against all but essential travel is 3.
t.Røde streger viser, hvilke lande der er: Red lines show which countries are in conflict with each other according to the media, and yellow lines who supports a country militarily. They are counted automatically every hour in GDELT, which reads news from around the world, but only mentions from our list of about 240 media outlets count. Large outlets that GDELT does not reach are read directly: Reuters, AP, CNN, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Post and more. A line is a suspicion (dashed) when at least 2 outlets have written about it within 7 days (30 days for military support). It becomes solid when at least 5 outlets from at least 3 countries outside the parties have written about it on at least 3 different days, and the articles have been read through. Only confirmed conflicts have a line on the globe. On the country page, the others get their line when you point at or tap the row. The lines run between the capitals, which are shown as small grey dots.
t.Vælger du et land, viser grønne streger,: When you choose a country, green lines show which countries and the EU have given at least USD 1 million in humanitarian aid this year, according to the UN Financial Tracking Service (OCHA FTS). For storms, a dashed line shows the storm's track from GDACS.
t.Hul og stiplet. Har intet alvorstal, før: Hollow and dashed. Has no severity until a source confirms or assesses it. Shown on the globe when you zoom in. Under Suspicions you choose whether they are shown.
t.Ring uden fyld. Smittestoffet er fundet: Ring without fill. The pathogen has been found in animals.
t.Alle smitteprikker er grønne. Trinnet st: All outbreak dots are green. The stage is shown in the list and in the details and shows how far the outbreak has progressed. The stage describes how the infection behaves. It does not say how many are affected or how great the risk is for you. Stages can be switched on and off under Area and stage in the side panel.
t.. Dokumenteret videregivelse fra person: . Documented transmission from person to person.
t.. Flere generationer af smitte, nye områ: . Several generations of transmission, new areas.
t.. Smittestof påvist hos dyr, ingen human: . Pathogen detected in animals, no human cases.
t.Kortet viser billede, kort fortalt, nøgl: The card shows an image, a summary, key figures, the timeline, sources and further reading. The arrows at the top browse on. Explore in the overview takes you through the most severe right now.
t.Alt, du kan trykke på, har en lille fork: Everything you can tap has a short explanation.
t.Kloden starter over det område, din inte: The globe starts over the area your internet connection appears to come from, and the Reset button takes you back there. The location is looked up by Cloudflare and not stored. The round pause button stops the rotation. It sits at the bottom right of the globe, above the zoom buttons, and on mobile above Reset. While a card is open, the globe stands still. After you have touched it, it waits 2 minutes and then takes 10 seconds to get up to speed, so you have time to stop it. Zoom with the mouse wheel, the buttons or two fingers, up to 40 times. Capitals get names from 2 times. The countries' regions fade in from 15 times and are fully shown from 25 times, with names from about 17 times.
t.På computer og Android: tryk Hent app øv: On computers and Android: tap Get app at the top when the button is there, or choose Install in the browser menu. On iPhone and iPad: tap Share in Safari and choose Add to Home Screen. The app opens in its own window and shows the most recently fetched data, also offline.
t.Under kloden vælger du, hvor alvorligt d: Below the globe you choose the minimum severity and when suspicions are shown. The ticker at the bottom shows severity 5 and 4. On mobile this is under Layers in the bottom bar, together with travel advice and the timeline.
t.Forstørrelsesglasset i overblikket søger: The magnifying glass in the overview searches by disease, place or event. The filter button chooses area and stage. On mobile, Search sits in the middle of the bottom bar and suggests places near you, countries you follow, your recent searches and popular topics.
t.Overblikket starter i hele verden. Vælg: The overview starts with the whole world. Choose an area, and the globe zooms there and shows what matters most, the directions and the countries in the area. The line at the top of the card shows the path, e.g. World › Africa › DR Congo › Ebola, and each step can be tapped. Drag the card down to go up a step, and swipe sideways for the next item on the same step.
t.Træk i den for at se en tidligere dato,: Drag it to see an earlier date, or tap Play the year.
t.Læg op til tre hændelser ved siden af hi: Put up to three events side by side with their curves.
t.Adressen følger den valgte hændelse, så: The address follows the selected event, so a link leads straight to it. The share button in the card gives a link that shows a title, text and image when shared on e.g. Facebook or Messenger.
t.Følg et land med stjernen, og tryk på kl: Follow a country with the star and tap the bell. You then get a notification on your phone or computer when the travel advice changes, or when there is a new outbreak, a warning from severity 3 or a confirmed conflict in the country. On iPhone and iPad, the page must first be added to the home screen. Only the browser's notification address and the countries are stored.
t.Knappen EN øverst (på mobilen under Lag): The EN button at the top (on mobile under Layers) shows the page in English. Buttons, headings and this guide are translated in advance. The summaries and timelines in the cards are machine translated and marked as such.
t.Et tal står, som kilden har opgjort det,: A figure is shown as the source counted it, with the source's reporting date when it is known. If a figure is missing, no source has counted it.
t.Oplysninger, der kun bygger på medier el: Information based only on media or secondary sources has not been confirmed by an authority.
t.markerer det, kilderne ikke har afklaret: marks what the sources have not clarified.
t.er sidens egen vurdering og bygger ikke: is the page's own assessment and is not based on a source.
t.Alt det, der er kommet til siden, med en: Everything that has been added to the page, with a short explanation. When something new is added, it appears first under What's new and here at the same time.
t.Få besked om de lande, du følger: Get notified about the countries you follow
t.Følg et land med stjernen, og tryk på kl: Follow a country with the star and tap the bell in the country's card. You then get a notification when the travel advice changes, or when there is a new outbreak, a warning from severity 3 or a confirmed conflict. On iPhone and iPad it works when the page is on the home screen as an app.
t.Knappen EN øverst (på mobilen under Lag): The EN button at the top (on mobile under Layers) shows the page in English. The summaries and timelines in the cards are machine translated and marked as machine translated. The language is chosen from your browser the first time.
t.Verden lige nu, når du kommer ind: The world right now when you arrive
t.Første gang du åbner siden, står det vig: The first time you open the page, the most important things right now are shown in three lines with a way into Explore.
t.Deler du en hændelse, et sted eller et l: When you share an event, a place or a country with the share button, the link now shows its own title, text and image, e.g. on Facebook and in Messenger.
t.På telefonen lukker Tilbage (og swipe ti: On phones, Back (and swiping back on iPhone) now closes search and Layers instead of leaving the page. Layers and Data and sources also show when each direction was last updated.
t.Kloden zoomer ind på det, du vælger: The globe zooms in on what you choose
t.Trykker du på et land, et område, et ste: When you tap a country, an area, a place or an event, the globe zooms in so that it fills the map with a little space around it. Choose Denmark and you see Denmark, not all of Northern Europe. An event is shown with its country, and an outbreak in several countries with all its places.
t.Kloden står stille, mens du kigger: The globe stands still while you look
t.Mens et kort er åbent, drejer kloden ikk: While a card is open, the globe does not turn. After you have touched it, it waits 2 minutes and then takes 10 seconds to get up to speed, so you have time to stop it where it is. The pause button now stands on its own at the top right of the globe.
t.På telefonen har siden nu en bjælke i bu: On phones the page now has a bar at the bottom like an app: Overview, Explore, Search, Following and Layers. Following shows the countries you follow, with a number when there is news. Layers gathers severity, suspicions, the timeline and travel advice, so the top only has the directions.
t.Søg midt i bundbjælken åbner en søgning,: Search in the middle of the bottom bar opens a full-screen search. Before you type, it suggests places near you, countries you follow, your recent searches and popular topics. As you type, countries and events appear straight away.
t.Fra verden til hændelsen, trin for trin: From the world to the event, step by step
t.På mobilen vælger du først et område, så: On mobile you first choose an area, then a country and then the individual place or event. The globe zooms along at each step. The line at the top of the card shows the path, e.g. World › Africa › DR Congo › Ebola. Drag the card down to go up a step.
t.Tryk på Prototypedata øverst, så ser du,: Tap Prototype data at the top to see which data the page fetches, from where and when it was last fetched, and the latest updates, ten at a time.
The star in the detail card follows the country. Countries you follow are at the top of the overview and are marked when something has changed since you last looked. This is stored only in your own browser.
t.Tryk på et land på kloden, så samles alt: Tap a country on the globe to gather everything about it in one place: travel advice, war and conflict, outbreaks, warnings, aid and refugees, with the highest severity at the top.
t.På landesiden giver RSS-knappen et feed: On the country page, the RSS button gives a feed for that country, which you can follow in your news reader. An item reappears when it changes.
t.Knappen med de to pile i detaljekortet g: The button with the two arrows in the detail card makes the card wide, with the content in two columns and the whole timeline as a horizontal line. The globe moves to the right so you can still see the place. Computers only.
t.Tryk på et punkt i forløbet for et smitt: Tap a point in an outbreak's timeline, and the timeline jumps to that date and the globe flies to the place. The Play the outbreak button goes through the whole timeline.
t.Øverst i overblikket står det, der er ko: The top of the overview shows what has been added or changed severity since your last visit. The dots have a small blue mark on the globe. The page remembers your last visit in your own browser.
t.Detaljekort med billede og læs mere: Detail card with image and further reading
t.Alle hændelser har nu samme kort: billed: All events now have the same card: image, summary, key figures, timeline, sources and three articles for further reading. For users in Denmark, the first article is from DR when DR has written about it.
t.Knappen Udforsk i overblikket tager dig: The Explore button in the overview takes you through the twelve most severe events right now, one card at a time. Browse with the arrows or by swiping on your phone.
t.Hent som app og ny mobil: Get as an app, and a new mobile view
t.Siden kan lægges på computeren eller tel: The page can be installed on your computer or phone as an app and also opens offline. Tap here to get it. On phones the map fills the whole screen, and the overview and details are pulled up from the bottom.
t.Alvor 5, akut, og søljen Lige nu: Severity 5, acute, and the Right now ticker
t.Det nye og kritiske lige nu har fået sit: What is new and critical right now has its own level, severity 5. It and severity 4 scroll in the ticker at the bottom of the page, and a tap takes you there.
t.Hvert sted, medierne skriver om kampe el: Each place where the media write about fighting or protests has its own dot. Tap the dot to see only what has been written about that place. Tap the country itself to open the country page.
t.Varslerne om krig og konflikt, jordskælv: Alerts about war and conflict, earthquakes, storms, floods, fires, heat and volcanoes are fetched automatically every hour from the sources' own feeds. Travel advice is fetched every 6 hours. If a source fails, its latest reports are shown until it responds again. Alerts are only shown for today, not back in time on the timeline. Further-reading articles are found every hour among the headlines of the major media and in GDELT. Images come from the Wikipedia article on the subject and are only used with a free licence from Wikimedia Commons.
t.Smitteudbruddene gennemgås automatisk fi: The outbreaks are reviewed automatically four times a day by fixed rules and a rota, so each part of the world gets its turn. The other directions are fetched every hour. What has changed, and on which source, is listed in
t.Ændringerne går på siden uden at være se: Changes go onto the page without first being checked by a person.
t.Siden er en prototype. Datasættet blev s: The page is a prototype. The dataset was compiled on 8 October 2026, and older points in the timelines do not yet have their own source. That is what the Prototype data label at the top of the page means.
The page does not cover every outbreak in the world. The normal season for known diseases is not included unless an authority calls it unusual.
t.Siden er en oversigt over, hvad kilderne: The page is an overview of what the sources have reported. It cannot be used to assess your own risk. If you are ill or in doubt, contact your doctor. If you are travelling, use the authorities' own advice:
t.For de andre retninger oversættes kilden: For the other directions, the source's own colour is translated: the Danish ministry's yellow, orange and red become 2, 3 and 4. USGS PAGER green, yellow, orange and red become 1 to 4, and an earthquake without a PAGER alert is 1. GDACS green, orange and red become 1, 3 and 4. Meteoalarm yellow, orange and red become 2, 3 and 4.
t.Vulkanudbrud med GDACS-varsel. Smithsoni: Volcanic eruptions with a GDACS alert. The Smithsonian's weekly report has been removed because it cannot be fetched automatically.
t.Hver retning har sit eget ikon og sin eg: Each direction has its own icon and colour. The buttons at the top switch them on and off, and the number shows how many events there are. A click switches a direction on or off, and a double click shows only that one. Travel advice and data centres are a service: their buttons stand apart on the right and are off until you switch them on.
t.Tryk på et ikon øverst for at slå retnin: Tap an icon at the top to switch the direction on or off. Double-click to see only that direction, and double-click again to go back. Travel advice and data centres stand apart on the right and are off until you switch them on. On mobile they are under Layers.
t.De største datacentre i verden: i drift,: The world's largest data centres: operating, under construction and planned
No data centres match the selected filters.
t.Brugere står kun, når en kilde nævner de: Users are only listed when a source names them. "Likely" is the source's own assessment.
t.De største datacentre i verden: i drift: The world's largest data centres: operating (filled dot), under construction (half filled) and planned or approved (dashed). The dot's area follows the IT power. Power, cost and water are often estimates and marked as such. The layer is not a risk and does not count towards severity or notifications.
t.Epoch AI (Frontier Data Centers), selska: Epoch AI (Frontier Data Centers), the companies' own information, authorities and OpenStreetMap
t.Datacentre: effekt, ejer, brugere og byg: Data centres: power, owner, users and construction progress for the largest AI sites. Estimates are marked. CC BY 4.0.
t.Knappen ved siden af rejsevejledningerne: The button next to travel advice (on mobile under Layers) shows the world's largest data centres: operating, under construction and planned. The dot's size follows the power. Tap a data centre for owner, users, consumption, timeline and sources.
